en.title: Microsoft Reportedly Shopping Halo and Other Franchises for TV & Movie Deals
en.summary: After a mixed reception to its flagship series, Microsoft is reportedly exploring new avenues to bring its biggest gaming IPs to the screen. The company is said to be pitching a slate of beloved franchises, including **Halo**, **The Elder Scrolls**, and **Diablo**, to various studios and streamers.
en.body:
Microsoft appears to be once again testing the waters for a major Hollywood push, with reports indicating they are actively seeking partners for a slate of their most iconic gaming franchises. Following the **Minecraft** movie's financial success and the critical reception of **Fallout**, the tech giant is reportedly looking to capitalize on its IP portfolio, even as the **Halo** TV series on Paramount+ garnered a lukewarm response from audiences and critics alike.

Puck News reported that **Microsoft** and **Xbox** have been holding meetings with multiple studios and streamers in recent weeks. The aim is to package a collection of their biggest gaming brands – including **The Elder Scrolls**, **Diablo**, **Warcraft**, and yes, **Halo** – in hopes of securing a significant deal. This strategy echoes the success **Nintendo** found with its **Super Mario Bros. Movie** and **Sony** achieved with **The Last of Us**, demonstrating a clear desire from **Microsoft** to replicate that kind of cross-media triumph.

## A Second Chance for the Master Chief?

The initial **Halo** series, which debuted in 2022, faced considerable challenges. While it boasted impressive production values, its narrative choices, particularly regarding Master Chief's character arc and the departure from established lore, proved divisive among the game's dedicated fanbase. Many felt the show strayed too far from the core tenets that made the **Halo** universe so beloved, leading to a sense of disappointment. Now, with **Microsoft** reportedly open to new adaptations, the question looms: can they find a showrunner and creative team capable of capturing the essence of **Halo** while forging a fresh, engaging story for television or film?

## What Fans Are Saying

The news has predictably sparked a flurry of discussion across fan communities and social media. Many are cautiously optimistic, hoping this renewed interest will lead to a more faithful or at least more compelling adaptation of their favorite franchises. Others express skepticism, questioning whether **Microsoft** truly understands what makes these games resonate with players. The desire for well-crafted stories that respect the source material is palpable, with fans eager to see **The Elder Scrolls** or **Diablo** brought to life with the same care and depth found in their respective games. The stakes are high, as a poorly handled adaptation could further alienate fans and damage the reputation of these storied franchises.

## What's Next

Details regarding specific studios or streamers **Microsoft** is in talks with, or potential timelines for any new projects, have not yet been announced. Fans will be watching closely for any official confirmations or further leaks regarding these ambitious adaptation plans.

content_raw: At the risk of engaging in the sort of kneejerk factionalism that’s kicked off so many bloody and fractious console wars over the years, we’ll note in passing that Microsoft has been struggling to hold its own in the latest one: The battle for Hollywood supremacy. The Xbox brand hasn’t been without its gaming adaptation successes, admittedly:  A Minecraft Movie crafted a gigantic stack of money back in April of 2025, while the Fallout  TV show has earned modest critical and commercial success. But the game studio is also still clearly smarting from the reception that greeted the TV version of one of its biggest brands of all time,  Halo , back in 2022, as audiences collectively shrugged at the weird and murky world of Paramount+’s TV version of the series. But you can’t keep a good slop merchant down, as Puck  recently reported ( per GamesRadar ) that Microsoft and Xbox are apparently doubling downs on plans to try to match the Hollywood success of Nintendo’s Mario  movies or Sony’s  The Last Of Us . The report states that Microsoft has been taking meetings with multiple studios and streamers in recent weeks, trying to spark interest in a whole greatest hits collection of the company’s gaming brands, including The Elder Scrolls ,  Diablo ,  Warcraft , and, hilariously,  Halo … again.  Puck  claims Microsoft is trying to sell the whole thing as a package deal that’ll bring a number of its gaming projects together in exchange for a big payday. And, let’s be fair: It  is a list of massive game franchises—but also one that speaks to the problem Microsoft has dug for itself here with the kind of gaming projects it tends to emphasize. Unlike Last Of Us or  Mario , or the upcoming  God Of War  show, or any number of the more successful video game adaptations of this most recent wave, none of the games Microsoft is reportedly peddling here are rooted in iconic and instantly recognizable characters. Movie fans already rejected the generic fantasy trappings of Warcraft   a decade ago; the Elder Scrolls  games are all about player freedom that will struggle to manifest in non-interactive forms; and Diablo , shorn of its compulsive gameplay loop, is less a collection of stories than it is a moving gallery of heavy metal album covers. It feels telling that Halo  was the most narratively developed out of any of these projects in gaming form, and its two-season TV run demonstrated that there wasn’t enough heft to either main character Master Chief. or the source material as a whole, to support a multi-season arc without a lot  of oddball invention on the showrunners’ parts. None of these are a deathknell, obviously:  Minecraft  doesn’t have a plot or real characters, and that didn’t stop it from chicken jockeying its way to nearly a billion dollars (and a planned sequel) last
